beats.on_screen: Cooking for 6? Don't add 50% to the time.
beats.vo: Scaling a recipe up? Multiply the ingredients. Not the minutes.
Amounts do scale. One and a half pounds of chicken becomes two and a quarter pounds.

beats.on_screen: More chicken needs batches, not time
beats.vo: Broiling fifty percent more chicken does not mean fifty percent longer. Use two batches, eight to ten minutes each.

beats.on_screen: Wider pan? Start checking at 10 minutes.
beats.vo: A wider pan reduces faster. Start checking at ten minutes. It is done when a spoon dragged through leaves a trail.
Swapped in coconut cream? Whisk it smooth, then keep the sauce at a gentle simmer.
This is a real RecipeFix result. It rewrote these steps, and said why.

beats.on_screen: Batches, not minutes. Cues, not clocks.
beats.vo: Scale the food, not the clock. Batches for space. Cues for doneness.

caption: Doubling a recipe, or cooking for more people? Multiply the ingredients, not the cook time. Give food room, and go by what you can see, like a spoon leaving a trail in the sauce.
